CHAPTER 8: VECTOR CONTROL
Sec. 8-1. Intent and application.
   The intent of this chapter is to protect the public health, safety and
welfare by preventing or controlling the spread of vector-borne disease through
the use of regulations, intervention, enforcement, education, advice and
assistance. Where practicable and not likely to cause injury to the public
health, in the sole opinion of the Director of Vector Control, the Vector
Control Department shall first attempt to use education, intervention, and
assistance to encourage voluntary compliance with the provisions of the
chapter.
   This chapter shall be applicable to all premises in unincorporated Richland
County regardless of the use or zoning classification. In instances where a
specific property use is regulated by the laws and regulations of the State of
South Carolina, the Vector Control Department shall work in conjunction with
the proper regulatory authority to remediate any violations of this chapter.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-2. Definitions.
   Harborage. Any area, interior or exterior, which is maintained in a manner
such that vectors will tend to live, nest, breed or seek shelter.
   Insect. Any of the numerous small invertebrate animals generally having the
body more or less obviously segmented, for the most part belonging to the Class
Insecta, comprising six-legged, usually winged forms, as for example, flies and
mosquitoes, and to other allied classes of arthropods whose members are
wingless and usually have more than six legs, as for example, spiders, and
ticks.
   Person. An individual, partnership, co-partnership, cooperative,
association, firm, company, public or private corporation, trust, estate, joint
structure company or any other legal entity or its legal representative, agent
or assigns.
   Premises. A parcel of real property, including all buildings and structures
located thereon. This term is used interchangeably with “Property.”
   Structure. All parts of a building, whether vacant or occupied, in all
stages of construction.
   Vector. An organism that has the ability to transmit disease, including, but
not limited to, mosquitoes, ticks, fleas, rats, etc.
   Waste. Garbage, household trash, debris, commercial waste, yard waste,
sewage, white goods, rubbish, paper, junk, building materials, glass or plastic
bottles, other glass, cans and any other discarded or abandoned material,
including solid, liquid, or semisolid matter.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-3. Minimum requirements.
   The provisions of this chapter shall govern the minimum requirements
required to keep premises in a clean and sanitary condition so as not to
adversely affect the public health or safety.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-4. Sanitation.
   All exterior property and premises shall be maintained in a clean, safe, and
sanitary condition to the extent necessary to prevent vector breeding and
harborage.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-5. Accumulation of waste.
   No person shall allow the accumulation or discharge of waste on any premises
to the extent and in such manner as to create a harborage or breeding ground
for rodents or other vectors.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-6. Insect and rodent harborage.
   (a)   All premises, structures, and exterior property shall be kept free
from insect and rodent harborage and infestation. All structures in which
insects or rodents are found shall be promptly exterminated in such manner as
will not be injurious to human health After pest and rodent elimination, proper
precautions shall be taken by (he occupant to prevent re-infestation.
   (b)   The accumulation of water in which mosquito larvae may breed is
prohibited.
   (c)   All premises shall be kept free from the excessive growth of weeds and
rank vegetation where mosquitoes harbor.
   (d)   The maintenance of any barn, stable, chicken yard, manure pile,
garbage receptacle, etc., in such manner that flies are in excess of reasonable
acceptable levels, as defined in the Vector Control Fly Protocol, as may from
time to time be amended, is prohibited.
   (e)   No dead animals or parts thereof shall be left on any exterior
premises for more than forty-eight (48) hours or thrown upon any street, road,
or public place.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-7. Swimming pools, spas, and hot tubs.
   Privately owned swimming pools, spas, and hot tubs shall be maintained in a
clean and sanitary condition to the extent and in such manner so as to prevent
vector breeding and harborage.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-8. Duty to abate.
   It shall be the duty of any owner, lessee, occupant, agent, or
representative of the owner of any property to comply with the requirements of
this chapter and take whatever action as may be necessary as often as may be
necessary to prevent the breeding and harborage of vectors.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
Sec. 8-9. Enforcement; Abatement; penalties.
   (a)   The Vector Control Director, or his/her authorized representative,
shall have the authority to investigate threats or potential threats to the
public health relating to vectors and potential vector transmitted diseases on
any premises in unincorporated Richland County and to require abatement of
conditions which violate the provisions of this chapter. As such, the Vector
Control Director, or his/her authorized representative, shall, with proper
consent, have the right of entry upon any premises where entry is necessary to
carry out the provisions of this chapter. If consent for entry is not given or
obtained by an authorized person, a search warrant shall be obtained by the
Vector Control Director from a court of competent jurisdiction before entry
onto the premises made.
   (b)   Whenever and wherever a condition shall exist which is determined by
the Vector Control Director, or his/her authorized representative, to be a
violation of this chapter, notice shall be given to the owner, lessee,
occupant, or agent or representative of the owner setting forth the violation,
and advising that the violation(s) must be corrected, the time allowed for such
correction, and the necessary methods or means to be employed in the
correction. It shall be sufficient notification to deliver the notice to the
person to whom it is addressed or to deposit a copy of such in the United
States mail, properly stamped, certified, and directed to the person to whom
the notice is addressed, or to post a copy of the notice upon such premises.
   (c)   Whenever and wherever a repeat violation of this chapter shall occur,
where more than one Uniform Ordinance Summons has been issued on the same
premises and/or on the same person, which, in the opinion of the Vector Control
Director, or his/her authorized representative, constitutes a public health
nuisance, it shall be his/her duty to notify in writing the person or persons,
firm or corporation, responsible for its continuance, of the character of the
public health nuisance and give the person, persons, firm, or corporation a
reasonable length of time to abate it. However, whenever and wherever a
nuisance is of a character as to require, in the interest of the public health,
immediate abatement or discontinuance, the Vector Control Director may bring a
proceeding for immediate action in the magistrate’s court for the abatement of
such nuisance and the court may upon hearing and for good cause enjoin the
continuance of the condition creating the nuisance, irrespective of all other
remedies at law.
   (d)   Any person who fails to abate the violation or public health nuisance
after notice shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor, issued a Uniform
Ordinance Summons, and, upon conviction, shall be subject to a fine not
exceeding five hundred dollars ($500.00) or imprisonment not exceeding thirty
(30) days, or both. Each day’s continuing violation shall constitute a separate
and distinct offense.
(Ord. No. 040-15HR, § I, 9-15-15)
CHAPTER 9: ELECTIONS*
   *Cross reference(s)--Administration generally,
Ch. 2; elected and special officers, §
2-262 et seq.
***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL *****
Sec. 9-1. Registration of electors.
   The books of registration shall be open from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday
through Friday at the office of the board of registration except during those
portions of the year in which such books are required to be closed.
(Code 1976, § 2-5001)
   State law reference(s)--Books to be kept open during hours other county
offices are normally open, S.C. Code 1976, § 7-5-130.
Sec. 9-2. Electoral districts.
   (A)   The county shall be divided into 11 new districts for the purpose of
electing members to the Council. Each new district shall be entitled to elect
one member of Council in accordance with S.C. Code 1976, § 4-9-90, as amended.
The new districts are as defined and delineated on the schedule of precincts
and voting districts, and as shown on the series of 11 maps, all of which are
herein adopted by reference.
   (B)   The County Attorney is hereby directed and authorized to submit the
plan for the new districts to the Attorney General of the United States for
preclearance pursuant to Section 5 of the U.S. Voting Rights Act of 1965, as
amended. The County Attorney is further directed to request expedited
preclearance in accordance with the regulations promulgated hereunder by the
Attorney General of the United States.
(Ord. No. 087-01HR, §§ II, III, 12-18-01; Ord. No. 003-02HR, §§ II, III, 1-29-
02)
** Secs. 9-3--9-12. Reserved. **
***** ARTICLE II. ELECTION COMMISSION *****
   Cross reference(s)--Boards, commissions and committees generally, § 2-326 et
seq.
Sec. 9-13. Employees and equipment--Limitation on outside work.
   Employees of the election commission are declared to be under the direction
of the county administrator and subject to the provisions of the personnel
ordinance. Election commission personnel may not perform any election-related
services, for pay or otherwise, for any town, city, party, union, or other
organization except pursuant to an agreement between the commission and such
organization for such services. No election commission personnel may accept any
money whatsoever from any political party, club, or organization. All
equipment, names, lists, data, and other materials belonging to the election
commission must remain in the commission office unless removed for a legitimate
purpose outlined in the directions or policies of the election commission.
(Code 1976, § 2-5002)
Sec. 9-14. Same--Overtime.
   If election commission or related personnel are required to work beyond
their normal work schedule for any election, they will be paid by the county at
their regular base rate for each hour of overtime.
   Unless such work is performed for a school or in a general or county special
election, the organization, city, town or party to which the services are
rendered must reimburse the county for all overtime and other extraordinary
expenses associated with such services.
(Code 1976, § 2-5003)
Sec. 9-15. Same--Outside use of voting machines.
   (a)   In the interests of voter education, colleges and schools will be
allowed to use voting machines in school elections or in displays at no charge.
A written request for the use of machines must be made two (2) weeks in advance
to the Richland County Election Commission, P.O. Box 4069, Columbia, South
Carolina 29240. This request must list all offices to be filled and all
candidates.
   (b)   Labor unions, fraternal organizations and other groups wishing to use
voting machines will be charged five dollars ($5.00) for each machine used. A
written request listing all offices and candidates will be required two (2)
weeks in advance.
   (c)   Any city (except the City of Columbia), town, or political party using
the machines for a municipal or primary election will be charged one dollar
($1.00) for each machine used (plus an optional five dollars ($5.00) per
machine charge for independent certification). The renter is responsible for
all costs of the programs, transportation, and for providing printed ballot
strips for the machine. Notice of all offices and candidates will be required
two (2) days after the filing deadline for the particular election.
(Code 1976, § 2-5004; Ord. No. 469-77, § 1, 12-7-77)
Sec. 9-16. Same--Damage to machines.
   If any machine is damaged while in the custody of any city, town, party,
school, or other organization using the machines, the cost of repairs will be
charged to that organization. If repairs can be made by the voting machine
custodian, the organization will be charged at the custodian's base pay rate
for each hour spent in repairing the machine, plus the actual cost of repair
parts.
(Code 1976, § 2-5005)
Sec. 9-17. Same--Election services.
   The election commission will contract with any city, town, or political
party in the county to provide services related to the holding of elections.
Upon the request of such city, town, or party, election commission personnel
will formulate an estimate of charges for the entire package of requested
services, based upon the actual unit costs of personnel, supplies, printing,
etc. Such charges may include the charge for providing voting machines as
specified above. After the election, the commission will render to the city,
town, or party a statement of charges which may vary from the estimated charge
only in the case of specific expenses or personnel time actually incurred
because of unanticipated events.
(Code 1976, § 2-5006)
Sec. 9-18. Same--Method of charging.
   All charges specified above will be remitted by check made payable to and
sent directly to the Richland County Finance Department, P.O. Box 4069,
Columbia, South Carolina 29240. All money remitted to the commission under
these provisions will be deposited with the finance department to the credit of
the general fund of Richland County.
(Code 1976, § 2-5007)
Sec. 9-19. Same--Priorities.
   If all requests for voting machines or election services cannot be filled
because of limited time or equipment, the following priorities will be
observed:
      (1)   General and county special elections;
      (2)   Municipal and primary elections;
      (3)   School and college elections; and
      (4)   Elections of unions, fraternal organizations, and other groups.
(Code 1976, § 2-5008)

CHAPTER 10: FIRE PREVENTION AND PROTECTION*
   *Editor’s note--By § I of Ord. No. 1164-84, the county entered into an
inter-governmental contract for fire protection with the City of Columbia.
Section IV prescribed for enforcement after the date of the contract between
the city and county, with implementation after Jan. 1, 1985.
   Cross reference(s)--Fire prevention code, §
6-113 et seq.
Sec. 10-1. Compliance with chapter provisions.
   No person shall kindle or maintain any open burning or authorize any such
fire to be kindled or maintained within the unincorporated areas of the county,
except as stated in this article.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-2. Open burning on the premises of private residences.
   Open burning of leaves, tree branches and yard trimmings originating on the
premises of private residences and burned on those premises shall be permitted
within “rural” zoning districts, as defined under the Richland County Land
Development Code, provided that any fire must be located not less than 75 feet
from any structure, road, or property line and adequate provision has been made
to prevent the fire from spreading to within 75 feet of any such structure,
road or property line. Open burning of leaves, tree branches, and yard
trimmings shall be prohibited on the premises of private residences within any
“residential” zoning district, as defined under the Richland County Land
Development Code.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-3. Open burning on the premises of undeveloped properties for the
purpose of land clearing or right-of-way maintenance.
   Open burning on the premises of undeveloped properties upon which no private
residence is situated, including undeveloped properties within “residential”
zoning districts, as defined under the Richland County Land Development Code,
for the purpose of land-clearing or right-of-way maintenance shall be
permitted, provided that such burning is conducted in accordance with the SC
Department of Health and Environmental Control (DHEC) Air Quality Regulations
61-62.2 and 61-62.4 and S.C. Code 1976, § 48-35-10 et seq. Open burning for the
purpose of land clearing and right-of-way maintenance shall be prohibited
during the ozone season (April 1 through October 30).
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-4. Attendant and fire extinguishing equipment required; notice to state
forester; adherence to state law.
   The burning must be constantly attended by a competent person until such
fire is extinguished. Such person shall have a garden hose connected to a water
supply, or other fire extinguishing equipment readily available for use. Proper
notification shall be given to the state forester or his duly authorized
representative or other persons designated by the state forester. The notice
shall contain all information required by the state forester or his
representative. The burning must be conducted in accordance with related state
laws and regulations including, but not limited to, DHEC Air Quality
Regulations 61-62.2 and 61-62.4 and S.C. Code 1976, § 48-35-10 et seq.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-5. Fires shall be prohibited as follows.
         a.   The county Fire Marshal may prohibit open burning when
atmospheric conditions, local circumstances or other conditions exist that
would make such fires hazardous.
         b.   The following materials shall not be burned in an open fire:
asphalt and asphaltic materials, paint, plastics, metals, treated wood, paper,
petroleum products, demolition debris, dead animals, construction debris,
household chemicals, household garbage, tires, trade waste and cardboard.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-6. Criteria for determining hazards.
   Reasonable criteria shall be established by the county council to assist in
determining when outdoor fires may be hazardous. These criteria may include air
quality standards as well as various fire danger indexes.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-7. Prohibited on county roads, drainage rights-of-way and adjacent
areas.
   Open burning shall be prohibited on all county roads and drainage rights-of-
way, or within an area that may cause damage to such areas.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-8. Exemptions.
         a.   This article does not apply to vegetative debris burning related
to forestry, wildlife and agricultural burns, as authorized by the state
forestry commission.
         b.   This article is not meant to restrict open burning in the
connection with the preparation of food for immediate consumption, or campfires
and fires used solely for recreational purposes, ceremonial occasions or human
warmth that are done in a safe manner.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-9. Restrictions; exceptions.
   Smoke production must be ended and no combustible material may be added to
the fire between official sunset of one day and official sunrise of the
following day with the exception of fires in the connection with the
preparation of food for immediate consumption, or campfires and fires used
solely for recreational purposes, ceremonial occasions, or human warmth and
fires where time parameters are already regulated by the Department of
Environmental Control Regulation 61-62.2.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-10. Hazardous or toxic materials.
   Hazardous or toxic materials shall not be burned.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-11. Permit for organized public fireworks displays--Fee.
   A charge of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) shall be made for the issuance of
the public fireworks display permit required by the fire prevention code
adopted in Article V of
Chapter 6, to cover administrative costs.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-12. Same--Disposition of fee.
   All fees required by section
10-2 shall be deposited in the county general fund, in accordance with the
receipts and deposits policies established by county council.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-13. Same--Penalties.
   Any person holding a fireworks display in the county without obtaining a
permit as provided in the fire prevention code adopted in Article V of
Chapter 6, shall be deemed in violation of S.C. Code 1976, § 23-35-60, as
amended, and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished according to law.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-14. Burning of structures for fire-fighting training.
   A vacant, dilapidated and unsafe structure may be burned by personnel of a
legally constituted fire department for fire-fighting training purposes. Before
such training is commenced, the appropriate fire department official will
present proof to the county building official that approval for burning the
structure has been obtained, if so required, from the state department of
health and environmental control and the owner of the structure. Upon
presentation of the required proof, the building official will issue a permit
for the burning of the structure. When the burning/training is completed, the
fire department which conducted the training will remove or cause to be removed
debris, burned or unburned, lying within ten feet of the perimeter wall of the
structure. Necessary and appropriate seeding will be accomplished to establish
vegetation to prevent transporting of soil to other people’s property by way of
erosion. On completion of the removal of debris and necessary seeding, the fire
department official will notify the building official, so that an inspection
will be made for compliance with this section and the closing out of the
permit.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-15. Civil and criminal liability.
   The authorization to conduct an open burn does not relieve the individual
responsible from civil or criminal liabilities resulting from the burning.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
Sec. 10-16. Conflicts of article with state law.
   The provision of this chapter shall prevail and be controlling over
provisions of state law if such is allowed by state law. Otherwise, if any
conflict arises between the provisions of this chapter and any state law, the
provisions of state law shall prevail and be controlling.
(Ord. No. 001-09, § I, 1-6-09)
CHAPTER 11: FRANCHISING REGULATIONS*
   *Cross reference(s)--Utilities,
Ch. 24.
***** ARTICLE I. IN GENERAL *****
** Secs. 11-1--11-10. Reserved. **
***** ARTICLE II. CABLE TELEVISION *****
   State law reference(s)--Authority to grant franchises, S.C. Code 1976, § 4-
9-30(11).
Sec. 11-11. Purpose.
   In order to better protect the public interest, welfare, and convenience,
the following article is hereby enacted, setting forth the conditions,
requirements, and limitations under which a person may construct, operate, and
maintain a cable antenna television system in this county. It is the express
intent of the county council that this article shall govern all cable antenna
television system franchises granted after November 3, 1992.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § I, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-12. Definitions.
   For the purpose of this article, the following terms, words, phrases, and
their derivations shall have the meanings given herein:
   Cable system, cable television system, or CATV system means a facility,
consisting of a set of closed transmission paths and associated signal
generation, reception, and control equipment that is designed to provide cable
service which includes video programming and which is provided to multiple
subscribers within a community, but such terms do not include: (1) A facility
that services only to retransmit the television signals of one or more
television broadcast stations; (2) A facility that serves only subscribers in
one or more multiple unit dwellings under common ownership, control, or
management, unless such facility or facilities uses any public right-of-way;
(3) A facility or common carrier which is subject, in whole or in part, to the
provisions of Title II of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, except
that such facility shall be considered a cable system (other than for purposes
of Section 621 (c) of the Cable Communications Policy Act of 1984) to the
extent such facility is used in the transmission of video programming directly
to subscribers; or (4) Any facilities of any electric utility used solely for
operating its electric utility systems.
   CATV shall mean Cable television.
   Council shall mean the County Council of the County of Richland.
   County shall mean the County of Richland, South Carolina.
   Department shall mean that department or agency of Richland County
designated by the County Administrator to supervise, monitor and implement a
cable television system franchise granted hereunder, including the enforcement
of its terms and provisions.
   Franchise shall mean and include the authorization, right or privilege to
construct, erect, operate and maintain in, upon, along or across public places
in the county, now laid out or dedicated, and all extensions thereof and
additions thereto, poles, wires, cables, underground conduits, manholes and
other conductors and fixtures necessary to maintain and operate a CATV system
in the county; provided, however, that such authorization in whatever terms
granted, shall not include any non-discriminatory license or permit as may be
required by the County of Richland for the privilege of operating a business
within the county. As used in this article, the term "franchise" shall not mean
the grant of an exclusive right to operate a cable television system in any
part of the county, unless so indicated.
   Franchise area shall mean the unincorporated area within the county.
   Franchisee shall mean the person to whom or to which a cable television
franchise is granted by the county.
   Franchise ordinance shall mean an ordinance granted by council to the
franchisee, granting the franchisee the right and privilege to construct and
operate a cable television system in the franchise area. If approved by
council, the franchise ordinance shall constitute proof of the grant of a
franchise.
   Gross revenue shall mean any and all revenues for periodic services, for
installations, relocations of outlets, and all compensation and other
consideration received from subscribers within the county, and revenues derived
from advertising sales based on the ration determined by dividing the number of
subscribers within the unincorporated county, by the total number of
subscribers served by the cable system; provided, however, that this shall not
include any taxes on grantee's services imposed directly upon any subscriber or
user by any governmental unit and collected by the grantee on behalf of said
governmental unit.
   Pay television shall mean the practice of transmitting any special program
or event for which a distinct charge is made to the subscriber in the manner
commonly known and referred to as "pay television," or to directly or
indirectly install, maintain, or operate on any television set a coin box or
any other device or means for collection of money for individual programs.
"Home Box Office," "Showtime," and like services are excluded from this
definition.
   Person shall mean any person, firm partnership, association, corporation,
company or organization of any kind.
   Property of the franchisee shall mean all property owned, leased, installed,
or used by the franchisee in the conduct of a cable television system.
   Rate shall mean all revenues for subscriber services whether received
directly or indirectly from a subscriber. It shall include all installation and
removal fees or charges.
   Street shall mean the surface of and space above and below any publicly
owned or maintained property or right-of-way, street, road, highway, freeway,
lane, path, alley, court, sidewalk, easement, parkway, or drive, now or
hereafter existing as such within the county.
   Subscriber shall mean any person or entity receiving for any purpose the
cable television service of the franchisee.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § II, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
   Cross reference(s)--Rules of construction and definitions generally, §
1-2.
Sec. 11-13. Compliance with applicable laws, ordinances, regulations, and
rules.
   In addition to the provisions of this article and the general police power
of the county and State of South Carolina, every franchise granted hereunder
shall be subject to the provisions of 47 United States Code Sections 521 et
seq., Sections 58-12-10 et seq. South Carolina Code of Laws, 1976, as amended,
and all federal and state regulations promulgated thereunder, and the county
may amend any franchise ordinance granted hereunder to incorporate the
provisions of amended statutes or regulations, including regulation to provide
consumer protection, protect consumer privacy and assure customer service, as
the county may adopt pursuant to the provisions of 47 U.S.C. Section 552 as
adopted heretofore or may be amended, upon terms mutually agreeable between the
county and the franchisee.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § III, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-14. Territorial area involved.
   A franchise granted under the provisions of this article shall extend to the
whole of the franchise area unless otherwise provided for by the franchise
ordinance.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § IV, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-15. Operation of franchise without a franchise ordinance prohibited.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to operate a cable television system in
the franchise area without a franchise ordinance.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § V, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 1779-88, § 17-28-88; Ord. No. 2264.1-
92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-16. Limits upon business interests.
   (a)   A franchisee under this article, its officers, agents, and/or
employees shall not directly or indirectly engage in the conduct of any
service, rental, leasing or retail business, including but not limited to,
television receivers, radio receivers, or related parts and accessories, or any
other business which may conflict with or detract from delivery of service
through its cable television system, nor shall any franchisee, its officers,
agents, and/or employees require or attempt to direct its subscribers, either
directly or indirectly, to deal with any firm or person in regard to sale,
service, rental, or leasing of television receivers, radio receivers, or
related parts and accessories. All restrictions upon additional business
interests of cable television franchisees contained in 47 United States Code
Section 521 et seq., statutes of the State of South Carolina, and/or
regulations promulgated thereunder shall be incorporated in all franchises
granted hereunder and/or by amendment to existing franchises, upon terms
mutually agreeable to the county and the franchisee.
   (b)   The franchise ordinance, unless it provides otherwise, only authorizes
the operation of a cable television franchise.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § VI, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-17. Franchise application procedure.
   (a)   Any person may apply to the council for the grant of a franchise.
   (b)   Such application shall be made on a form supplied by the county. In
the absence of any prescribed form, the applicant may apply by filing a neat,
legible, typewritten letter of application with the council.
   (c)   The applicant shall furnish such further information as shall be
requested by the council as to ownership, affiliations, finances, proposed
operating information, rate structure, and such other relevant information as
the council shall request.
   (d)   The applicant shall forward with its application a nonrefundable
application fee of five hundred dollars ($500.00).
   (e)   During the period in which an application is pending before the
council, the applicant shall immediately inform council of any change in the
information previously furnished.
   (f)   In considering the application for a franchise, the council, in its
deliberations, shall take into consideration, among other factors it deems
appropriate, the following factors:
      (1)   Need for service;
      (2)   Ability of the applicant to provide service in an effective and
satisfactory manner;
      (3)   Public health, welfare, and safety of residents of the area to be
served;
      (4)   Economic impact on the area and the county as a whole;
      (5)   The most feasible means of providing service; and
      (6)   The general background and record of the applicant.
   (g)   The application shall be approved or rejected by the council after a
review of the application, consideration of the above factors, and any other
information deemed relevant, following three (3) readings and a public hearing.
   (h)   The county shall have the right to make a public invitation for bids
on a franchise within the franchise area.
   (i)   Nothing in this article shall prohibit the county from issuing and
granting different franchises with the same technical and performance standards
to different parties within the franchise area, where such differentiation is
in the best interests of the citizens of the county.
   (j)   The council shall process promptly and render a determination within
six (6) months of the filing of such application.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § VII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92))
Sec. 11-18. Grant of franchise.
   (a)   Generally. The grant of a franchise shall entitle the franchisee to
the right and privilege to construct, erect, operate, and maintain, in, upon,
along, across, above, over, and under the streets, alleys, public ways, and
public places not laid out or dedicated, and all extensions thereof, and
additions thereto, in the county, poles, wires, cables, underground conduits,
manholes, and other television conductors and fixtures necessary for the
maintenance and operation in the county of a CATV system for the interception,
sale, and distribution of television and radio signals.
   (b)   Term. The term of franchises granted hereunder shall be as prescribed
by franchising ordinance, but in no case shall the term of any franchise exceed
a period of fifteen (15) years from and after the date of approval by the
county council.
   (c)   Liability and indemnification.
      (1)   Liability of the county shall in every case be governed by the
South Carolina Tort Claims Act, Sections 15-78-10 et seq. South Carolina Code
of Laws (1976, as amended). In every case, the franchisee shall indemnify the
county for any and all damages and penalties the county may legally be required
to pay as a result of the franchisee's actions. These damages or penalties
shall include, but shall not be limited to, damages arising out of copyright
infringements and all other damages arising out of the installation, operation,
or maintenance of the cable television system authorized by the franchise
ordinance whether tort, contract, or products liability, and whether or not any
act or omission complained of is authorized or allowed, or prohibited by the
franchise ordinance.
      (2)   Nothing in this article shall be construed or interpreted as an
extension of any immunity enjoyed or owned by the county to the franchisee.
      (3)   The franchisee shall maintain, and by its acceptance of a
franchise, specifically agrees that it will maintain throughout the terms of
its franchise adequate liability insurance insuring the county and the
franchisee with regard to all damages as prescribed by the South Carolina Tort
Claims Act, Section 15-78-120 South Carolina Code of Laws, (1976, as amended).
      (4)   The franchisee shall maintain, and by its acceptance of a franchise
shall specifically agree, that it will maintain throughout the first two (2)
years of its franchise a faithful performance bond running to the county, with
at least two (2) good and sufficient sureties approved by the county, in the
sum which council shall deem reasonable that the franchisee shall well and
truly observe, fulfill, and perform each term and condition of its franchise
and that in case of any breach of condition of the bond, the amount thereof
shall be recoverable from the principal and sureties thereof by the county for
all damages proximately resulting from the failure of the franchisee to well
and faithfully observe and perform any provision of its franchise; provided,
however, that, the franchisee shall only be required to provide one surety if
that surety is a commercial bonding company. This provision does not apply to
renewal franchises.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § VIII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-19. Service to be commenced promptly; deadlines.
   (a)   Within thirty (30) days after the effective date of its franchise
agreement ordinance, a franchisee under this article shall proceed with all due
diligence to obtain all necessary permits and authorizations which are required
in the conduct of its business, including but not limited to, any utility joint
use attachment agreements, licenses, and authorizations required by duly
constituted regulatory agencies having jurisdiction over the operation of cable
television systems and service, including the obtaining of a certificate of
compliance from the Federal Communications Commission.
   (b)   Within ninety (90) days after obtaining all necessary permits, pole
permits, easements, licenses, and authorizations, including the certificate of
compliance issued by the Federal Communications Commission, the franchisee
shall commence construction and installation of the cable television system.
   (c)   Within two hundred seventy (270) days after the commencement of the
construction and installation of the cable television system, the franchisee
shall begin to render service to its customers.
   (d)   A franchisee's failure to commence and diligently pursue each of the
requirements set forth in paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section shall
constitute grounds for revocation of its franchise agreement; provided,
however, the council may extend the time for the commencement and completion of
construction and installation of service for additional service for additional
periods in the event the franchisee, acting in good faith, experiences delays
by reason of circumstances beyond its control.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § IX, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-20. System construction and extension.
   (a)   Whenever the franchisee receives requests for service from at least
sixty (60) subscribers within one mile of its aerial trunk cable, or from at
least one hundred (100) subscribers within one mile of its underground trunk
cable, it shall extend its system to such subscribers solely for the usual
connection and service fees for all subscribers, provided that such extension
is technically feasible. The one mile shall be measured in extension length of
company's cable required for service located within the public way or easement
and shall not include length of necessary service drop to the subscriber's home
or premises.
   (b)   No person in the franchisee's service area shall be arbitrarily
refused service; but in recognition of the capital costs involved in unusual
circumstances, including, without limitation, when the distance from
distribution cable to connection of service to subscribers is more than one
hundred fifty (150) feet, or when a subscriber density exists less than the
density specified hereinabove, or where a customer requests special service,
service may be made available on the basis of costs of materials, labor, and
easements, in order to prevent inequitable burdens on potential cable
subscribers in more densely populated areas.
   (c)   For all residential structures hereinafter erected which are to be
served by underground utilities, the developer of the subdivision or
development may acquire CATV service for his development under the following
conditions; but otherwise the franchisee shall not be obligated to construct a
CATV system in such new development. Such developer shall perform all trenching
and backfilling necessary for the provision of cable television service,
including furnishing of any imported backfill material required, and will
furnish and install for the franchisee any necessary distribution conduit and
substructures, including pedestals, required in accordance with the
franchisee's plans and specifications. In addition to providing plans and
specifications to the developer, the franchisee shall inspect the facilities
required hereunder, and certify to the county prior to final approval of the
subdivision or development that the facilities required herein are properly
installed. The county shall have the right to review and require its approval
of the maps and specifications provided by the franchisee. The cost of that
portion of an extension to a subdivision or development from the franchisee's
existing facilities in excess of two hundred (200) feet outside of the
boundaries of the subdivision or development shall be borne by the developer.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § X, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-21. Franchise fee.
   (a)   In consideration of the rights and privileges granted by its
franchise, each franchisee shall pay to the county a franchise fee of at least
five (5) per cent of its gross revenues annually or such franchise fee as may
be permitted under the provisions of 47 United States Code Section 521 et seq.,
regulations promulgated thereunder or as amended.
   (b)   The fee shall be payable annually on June thirtieth, for the preceding
year.
   (c)   The franchisee shall pay the county interest at the legal rate
permissible upon judgment per month for any balance of the franchise fee
payment left unpaid after June thirtieth of any given year. Failure of a
franchisee to pay the fee in full within ninety (90) days after June thirtieth
shall be deemed a default of a material obligation of the franchise. The
franchisee shall pay to the county all costs of collection with respect to fees
in arrears, including but not limited to court costs and reasonable attorney
fees.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XI, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 1658, § 1, 7-28-87; Ord. No. 2264.1-
92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-22. Conditions of street occupancy.
   (a)   The poles, towers, and other structures and appurtenances used by a
franchisee under this article, its successors and assigns, for the erection,
installation, construction, operation and maintenance of its cable television
system shall be so located and constructed as not to interfere with the traffic
over the streets and alleys, and the location of poles, towers, and all other
structures and installations shall be subject to the prior written approval and
under the supervision of the county, whenever the county shall so direct, as to
such locations, giving consideration to the reasonable operation of the same;
provided, further, that such location initially approved and used shall not be
considered a vested interest or privilege, and such structures, poles, and
other installations shall be removed and relocated by the franchisee whenever
the same shall restrict or obstruct the reasonable use of such streets, alleys,
and public places.
   (b)   A franchisee is also authorized to attach or otherwise affix cables or
wires to the facilities of any public utility even though the same may cross
over the streets, sidewalks, public lands and highways of the county; provided
that, the franchisee first secures the permission and consent of the
aforementioned public utility to affix the same cables, wires, or other
apparatus to the facilities of such public utility.
   (c)   All streets, sidewalks, alleys, and public highways disturbed or
damaged in the construction, operation, repair, relocation, or maintenance of a
cable television system shall be promptly repaired by the franchisee at its own
expense and to the complete satisfaction of the county.
   (d)   The franchisee shall, on the request of any person holding a building
moving permit issued by the county, temporarily raise or lower its wires to
permit the moving of buildings. The expense of such temporary removal or
raising or lowering wires shall be paid by the person requesting the same, and
the franchisee shall have the authority to require such payment in advance. The
franchisee shall be given a reasonable advanced notice to arrange for such
temporary wire changes.
   (e)   The franchisee shall have the responsibility and authority to trim
trees upon and overhanging streets, alleys, sidewalks, and public ways and
places of the county so as to prevent the branches of such trees from coming in
contact with the wires and cables of the franchisee.
   (f)   In all sections of the county where the cables, wires, or other like
facilities of public utilities are placed underground, the franchisee shall
place its cables, wires, or other like facilities underground to the maximum
extent that existing technology reasonably permits the franchisee to do so;
provided, however, that the franchisee shall not install underground cables,
wires, or other equipment on private property without the written consent of
the owner.
   (g)   No franchisee shall obtain any exclusive right to the use of any
utility pole, equipment, or facilities used by the franchisee in its
operations.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-23. Preferential or discriminatory practices prohibited.
   (a)   A franchisee under this article shall not discriminate as to rates,
charges, services, service facilities, rules, regulations, or in any other
respect make or grant any undue preference or advantage to any person.
   (b)   All franchisees shall sign and file with the clerk of council an equal
employment opportunity statement and shall so advertise as an equal employment
employer.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XIII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-24. Repealed.
Sec. 11-25. Standards of service.
   (a)   Generally. During the existence of its franchise, a franchisee under
this article shall furnish reasonable, adequate, and efficient cable television
reception service to its subscribers connected to its system within the county
and shall maintain its system in reasonable repair and working order at all
times.
   (b)   Number of channels required.
      (1)   Unless otherwise provided in the franchise ordinance or by law, the
franchisee shall establish a cable television system capable of providing the
maximum number of channels required or recommended by the provisions of 47
United States Code Sections 521 et seq. and regulations promulgated thereunder.
      (2)   The franchisee may include a selection of FM radio stations and
shall include services such as weather, time, and news.
   (c)   Color television.
      (1)   The facilities used by the franchisee shall be capable of
distributing color television signals.
      (2)   When the franchisee receives signals in color, they shall be
distributed in color where technically feasible as determined by the prevailing
standards of the industry.
   (d)   Signal quality requirements. The franchisee shall, under all
circumstances within its control:
      (1)   Produce a picture, whether in black and white or in color, that is
undistorted, free from ghost images, and accompanied with proper sound on
typical standard production TV sets in good repair, and as good as the state of
the art allows;
      (2)   Transmit signals of adequate strength to produce good pictures with
good sound at all outlets without causing cross-modulation in the cables or
interfering with other electrical or electronic systems;
      (3)   Demonstrate both by instruments and visually to subscribers that a
signal of adequate strength and quality is being delivered;
      (4)   Comply with the applicable standards of all federal and state
regulations, including, but not limited to, all such standards established by
the Federal Communications Commission.
   (e)   Operation and maintenance of system.
      (1)   A franchisee under this article shall render efficient service,
make repairs promptly, and interrupt service only for good cause and for the
shortest time possible.
      (2)   A franchisee under this article shall at all times keep and
maintain in the county a proper, sufficient and adequate inventory of
maintenance and repair parts for the cable television system as will assure the
continuity of the service of the system to subscribers in the county on a
prompt and efficient basis and without being subjected to delays by having to
obtain necessary parts and equipment from distant points; and a franchisee
shall keep available in the county at all times maintenance and repair crews in
sufficient number and capability as may be necessary and sufficient to give
prompt, reasonable, and capable maintenance and repair service to the cable
television system in accordance with good engineering practices. A franchisee
shall provide such adjustments and repairs as are necessary to provide a
quality signal to the subscriber within two (2) days of the time the report of
trouble is made, and repairmen shall be available for such purpose during
normal business hours and on an emergency basis, and must respond to a call
within twenty-four (24) hours after such call is received. A franchisee shall
place a higher priority on servicing existing customers with a quality signal
than hooking up new customers.
   (f)   Program alteration. All programs of broadcasting stations carried by
the franchisee shall be carried in their entirety as received, without
announcements and advertisements and without additions.
   (g)   Service to public buildings, schools, and teaching stations.
      (1)   The franchisee shall provide, without charge, one outlet to each
public building and fire station, within one hundred fifty (150) feet of its
existing trunk line, upon the request of the county or its designee.
      (2)   A franchisee under this article shall also provide, without charge,
one outlet to each public school and teaching station, within one hundred fifty
(150) feet of its existing trunk line, for educational purposes upon request by
the county and at no cost to the public school system.
      (3)   Should any such building be more than one hundred fifty (150) feet
from existing trunk lines and request service, free outlets shall be provided
where payment is made to franchisee for extra costs involved for connection and
a reasonable period of time allowed for service to be commenced.
      (4)   The distribution of the cable facility inside such buildings and
the extension thereof shall be at the option, duty, and expense of the building
owner.
   (h)   Removal of facilities upon request. Upon termination of service to any
subscriber, upon request, the franchisee shall promptly remove all of its
facilities and equipment from the property of such subscriber.
   (i)   Public access channel. At the request of council, a franchisee shall
provide at least one full-time composite access channel for educational,
governmental, and public uses. This channel shall be made available during the
hours from 9:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and during the hours
from 5:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m., Saturday and Sunday. No facilities or equipment
shall be required.
   (j)   Emergency service. In the event of an emergency or disaster, the
franchisee, upon the request of council, shall make available its facilities to
the county for emergency use during the emergency or disaster period.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XV, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-26. Safety regulations.
   (a)   A franchisee under this article shall at all times employ ordinary
care and shall install and maintain in use commonly accepted methods and
devices for preventing failures and accidents which are likely to cause
damages, injuries, or nuisances to the public.
   (b)   The franchisee shall install and maintain its wires, cables, fixtures,
and other equipment in accordance with the requirements of the National
Electrical Code of the National Board of Fire Underwriters, and in such manner
that they will not interfere with an installation of the county or of a public
utility serving the county.
   (c)   All structures and all lines, equipment, and connections in, over,
under and upon the streets, sidewalks, alleys, and public ways or places of the
county, wherever situated or located, shall at all times be kept and maintained
in a safe, suitable, substantial condition, and in good order and repair.
   (d)   A franchisee under this article shall maintain a force of one or more
resident agents or employees at all times and shall have sufficient employees
to provide safe, adequate, and prompt service for its facilities.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XVI, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-27. Transfer of franchise.
   A franchisee under this article shall not transfer its franchise without
prior approval of the council.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XVII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-28. Change of control of franchisee.
   Prior approval of the council shall be required where ownership or control
of more than five (5) per cent of the right of control of a franchisee is
acquired by a person or group of persons acting in concert, none of whom
already own or control five (5) per cent or more or such right of control,
singularly or collectively. By its acceptance of a franchise, a franchisee
shall specifically grant and agree that any such acquisition occurring without
prior approval of the council shall constitute a violation of the franchise by
the franchisee.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XVIII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-29. Filings and communications with regulatory agencies.
   Upon written request of the council, copies of all petitions, applications,
and communications submitted by a franchisee to the Federal Communications
Commission, Securities and Exchange Commission, or any other federal or state
regulatory commission or agency having jurisdiction in respect to any matters
affecting CATV operations authorized pursuant to the franchise, shall also be
submitted simultaneously to the council.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XIX, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-30. Records and reports.
   (a)   The county shall have access at all reasonable hours to all of a
company's plans, contracts, and engineering, accounting, financial,
statistical, customer and service records relating to the property and the
operation of such franchisee and to all other records required to be kept by
the franchise agreement ordinance, or state or federal regulation.
   (b)   When requested by council, a franchisee shall file with the clerk of
council true and accurate maps or plats of all existing and proposed
installations.
   (c)   When requested by council, a franchisee shall forward to the clerk of
council a copy of its report to its stockholders (if it prepares such a
report), an income statement applicable to its operations during the preceding
twelve (12) month period, a balance sheet, and a statement of its properties
devoted to CATV operations, by categories, giving its investment in such
properties on the basis of original cost, less applicable depreciation, or such
other information as may be requested.
   (d)   Not later than sixty (60) days thereafter, a franchisee shall, upon
request of council, file a written report with the council and shall,
thereafter, if and upon request by the council, appear before council and
discuss that written report and answer such questions as may be prompted by
that report. The report will relate to operations of the company during the
preceding calendar year and shall include, but not necessarily be limited to,
the following:
      (1)   Construction activities of the franchisee.
      (2)   Operating and service maintenance activities of the franchisee.
      (3)   Progress made by the franchisee in extending its service throughout
the county.
      (4)   The number of service maintenance calls made by the franchisee's
personnel, the average response time, the nature of any major cable reception
problems, and the approximate length of time required to service those major
cable reception problems.
      (5)   Activities of the franchisee designed to improve the quality of
maintenance and service.
      (6)   Future plans of the franchisee for the extension of its service to
new areas within the county limits.
      (7)   Plans of the franchisee for the future expansion and improvements
of the quality of service and maintenance to subscribers.
      (8)   Such other information as the council may direct the franchisee to
include in the report, or that the franchisee believes to be appropriate for
inclusion in the report.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XX, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-31. Rates.
   The county shall adopt such regulations and terms with respect to charges
and rates for cable television service as may be proper and permissible under
the provisions of 47 United States Code Section 543 as adopted heretofore or as
may be amended.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXI, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-32. Effect of franchisee's bankruptcy or insolvency.
   In the event a franchisee under this article shall be adjudicated bankrupt
or placed in receivership or make an assignment for the benefit of its
creditors, or any foreclosure or any mortgage or deed of trust upon its
properties shall be commenced, or any other insolvency proceedings either
voluntarily or involuntarily on the part of the franchisee shall be commenced,
the county may declare the franchise grant immediately terminated and in that
event all of the rights, privileges, and authority of the franchisee shall
immediately cease and terminate. In no event shall such franchise grant be
considered an asset of the bankrupt estate or receivership.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-33. Office in county required.
   (a)   A franchisee under this article shall maintain an office in the county
to which all notices, correspondence, complaints, and other communications from
the county shall be sent.
   (b)   The franchisee shall provide the county with official notification of
the location of the office.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXIII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-34. Personnel, services, and equipment required at local office.
   (a)   A franchisee under this article shall maintain through its local
office:
      (1)   A representative who shall be fully authorized and shall make
prompt investigations and resolutions of all complaints regarding the quality
of service, equipment malfunction, the handling of held orders for service, and
all other matters relating to or affecting the quality of service being
rendered and to be rendered by the franchisee in the operation of a cable
television system in the county.
      (2)   At least one standby local technician shall be available to respond
to any outages and other problems which occur at times other than the normal
working days.
   (b)   The franchisee shall maintain in its local office a listed telephone
which shall be operated, at which complaints and requests for repairs or
adjustments may be made at the franchisee's local office.
   (c)   A franchisee under this article shall maintain an answering service to
accept calls after normal business hours.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXIV, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-35. Response to requests for service.
   (a)   A franchisee under this article shall respond to all service calls
within a reasonable period of time. A reasonable period shall normally be
defined as twenty-four (24) hours for an initial response.
   (b)   In any event, the franchisee shall correct all malfunctions within a
reasonable period after the receipt of a request for service or complaint. For
the purposes of this paragraph (b), a reasonable period shall normally be
defined as seventy-two (72) hours.
   (c)   Normally, all installation requests shall be fulfilled within one week
of receipt where cable television is available, unless delayed by conditions
beyond the control of the franchisee or an unusual volume of requests, in which
case installation shall be completed as soon as reasonably possible.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXV, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-36. Complaints.
   (a)   All complaints received from the public shall be kept on file with the
clerk of council. The clerk of council shall forward to the franchisee a copy
of all complaints about the franchisee received by the clerk's office.
   (b)   All complaints received by the clerk of council shall be kept on file
for the life of the franchise agreement. Such complaints shall constitute a
public record and be open for inspection and copying by members of the public.
   (c)   There is hereby established a citizens oversight committee to consist
of seven (7) members, including not more than three (3) members nominated by
cable television franchisees, appointed on a staggered basis by the county
council for two (2) year terms, except that three (3) original members shall
serve one (1) year terms so that appointments and re-appointments shall be made
every year thereafter, alternating between three (3) and four (4) seats to be
filled each year. The functions of the committee shall be:
      (1)   To monitor consumer service standards;
      (2)   To advise the grantee on matters of subscriber service;
      (3)   To oversee cable television performance;
      (4)   To advise county council on consumer problems and suggestions.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXVI, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-37. Grounds for termination of a franchise.
   The county council may terminate a franchise and all rights and privileges
pertaining to it prior to its normal expiration on any or all of the following
grounds:
      (1)   The franchisee has made a material, false statement in the
application for the franchise, knowing it to be false;
      (2)   The franchisee, contrary to the best interest of public convenience
and welfare, is failing to provide subscribers with regular, adequate,
reasonable and proper service, as defined by generally accepted industry
standards;
      (3)   The franchisee has failed to comply with any material provision of
this article, or has defaulted in any of its material obligations hereunder,
except for causes beyond its control;
      (4)   The franchisee has failed within sixty (60) days after written
notice, or within such extended period as may be allowed by the county to
complete the correction of any default and remedy any noncompliance with the
provisions of this article or the franchise ordinance;
      (5)   The franchisee has violated any provisions of any relevant federal,
state or local law;
      (6)   The franchisee has failed to provide adequate cable service as
determined by the existing industry standards or becomes insolvent or is
adjudged bankrupt;
      (7)   The franchisee has consistently failed to respond to bona fide
complaints;
      (8)   Upon application of the franchisee and approval of council after a
public hearing.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXVII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-38. When a hearing shall be held.
   A public hearing shall be held on motion of council, or whenever the county
administrator has reason to believe that a franchisee under this article has
violated federal, state, or local law or has failed to provide adequate
service, or otherwise has failed to comply with the terms of this article or
its franchise ordinance.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXVIII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-39. Procedure for termination of a franchise.
   (a)   A franchise shall only be terminated after a public hearing and upon
approval of the county.
   (b)   A franchisee under this article shall have the following rights:
      (1)   Right to sixty (60) days' written notice setting forth the reasons
that a termination hearing is being held;
      (2)   Right to examine, and make copies at franchisee's expense of all
evidence which the county has, whether favorable or adverse to the franchisee;
      (3)   Right to be represented by counsel;
      (4)   Right to cross-examine witnesses;
      (5)   Right to present witnesses;
      (6)   Right to present evidence in its own behalf;
      (7)   A written decision setting forth council's decision.
   (c)   If council finds by a preponderance of the evidence that any of the
provisions of this article or state, local, or federal law, or the franchisee's
franchise ordinance has been violated, it may revoke the franchise agreement,
place on probation for a stated period of time, impose a civil penalty of not
more than five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) where circumstances are blatant, or
take such lawful action as it shall deem appropriate.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXIX, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-40. Hearing officer.
   Prior to any public hearing required or prescribed by any section of this
article, the county council may, in conjunction with the affected franchisee or
franchisees, appoint a mutually acceptable hearing officer who shall make
findings and recommendations, which findings and recommendations shall not be
binding upon the council; provided, however, that, if the county and the
affected franchisee(s) are unable to agree upon a mutually acceptable hearing
officer within twenty (20) days of the county's decision to appoint same, the
county and the affected franchisee shall each name one impartial hearing
officer and these persons shall agree upon a third hearing officer, within
twenty (20) days of their appointment, failing which, they shall discharge the
duties of the hearing officer; provided, further, that, the record presented
before the hearing officer(s) shall form the basis for the council's
consideration of the matter before it, and all parties will be bound by the
record, including testimony and exhibits.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXX, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-41. Removal of discontinued facilities.
   In the event that the use of any part of a cable television system is
discontinued for any reason for a continuous period of twelve (12) months, or
the franchise grant has been terminated, cancelled, revoked or has expired, the
franchisee shall promptly remove from the streets and public places and from
underground facilities under public streets and public places all such property
and poles, wires, conduits, vaults, and other parts of the system, other than
those which the county may permit to be abandoned in place, and, shall either
restore the street and the underground area or pay the county for restoring the
street or other area from which such property has been removed, to a condition
for public use acceptable to the county. Any property remaining in place for a
period of one hundred eighty (180) days after the termination or expiration of
a franchise ordinance shall be considered permanently abandoned, and may be
appropriated by the county or removed by the county at the expense of the
franchisee and the surety on its performance bond.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXXI, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-42. Subscriber refunds on termination of service.
   If any subscriber because of a franchisee's failure to render service to
such subscriber of a type and quality provided for by law, or if service to a
subscriber of less than three (3) years is terminated by franchisee without
good cause or because the franchisee ceases to operate the CATV business
authorized by this article and franchise ordinance for any reason, except
expiration of its franchise, the franchisee shall refund to each such
subscriber an amount equal to the initial tap-in and connection charges paid by
him divided by thirty-six (36) and multiplied by a number equal to thirty-six
(36) minus the number of months the subscriber has been on the system.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXXII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-43. Publication costs.
   A franchisee under this article shall assume the cost of publication of his
franchise as such publication is required by law and such is payable upon the
franchisee's filing of acceptance of his franchise.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXIII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-44. Penalty for unlawful interference.
   (a)   It shall be unlawful for any person to construct, install, or maintain
within any public street or roadway in the county, or within any other public
property of the county, or within any privately owned area within the county
which has not yet become a public street on any tentative subdivision which may
be approved by the county, any equipment or facilities for distributing any
television signals or radio signals through a CATV system, unless a franchise
authorizing such use of such street or property or area has first been
obtained, and unless such franchise is in full force and effect.
   (b)   It shall be unlawful for any person to make unauthorized connection,
whether physically, electrically, acoustically, inductively, or otherwise, with
any part of a franchise CATV system within this county for the purpose of
enabling anyone to receive any television signal, radio signal, picture, sound,
or other transmission, without payment to the company.
   (c)   It shall be unlawful for any person, without the consent of the owner,
to wilfully tamper with, remove, or injure any cables, wires or equipment used
for distribution of television signals, radio signals, pictures, sound, or
other transmission.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXIV, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-45. No waiver of right of eminent domain.
   Nothing in this article shall be construed as a waiver of the county's right
to exercise eminent domain.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXVI, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
Sec. 11-46. Effect on conflicting ordinances.
   All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict with the provisions of
this article are hereby repealed, with the exception of the cablevision
franchise ordinances which became effective prior to October 20, 1992.
(Ord. No. 773-81, § XXXVIII, 2-4-81; Ord. No. 2264.1-92HR, § I, 10-20-92)
CHAPTER 12: SOLID WASTE, RECYCLING, AND PUBLIC SANITATION
***** ARTICLE I. ADMINISTRATION *****
Sec. 12-1. In general.
   Richland County shall manage the solid waste stream on behalf of its
citizens in order to preserve and protect public health and welfare and to
promote a suitable quality of life for residents and visitors. It shall perform
these missions with appropriate staff, equipment, programs, and facilities and
in accordance with applicable federal and state laws and regulations. The task
of solid waste management shall be discharged by the Director of Public Works.
(Ord. No. 008-22HR, § I, 4-5-22)
Sec. 12-2. Definitions.
   Any definitions contained herein shall apply unless specifically stated
otherwise. In addition to the definitions contained in this chapter, the
articles of this chapter shall adopt by reference the definition of terms (to
the extent they are not inconsistent with definitions specifically contained
herein) defined in the South Carolina Solid Waste Policy and Management Act of
1991, South Carolina Code Section 44-96-10, et seq. and in any regulations
promulgated pursuant thereto. Any term not specifically defined will be
construed pursuant to its plain and ordinary meaning. When not inconsistent
with the context, words used in the present tense include the future, words
used in the plural include the singular, and words used in the singular include
the plural. The word "shall" is always mandatory and not merely discretionary.
   Agricultural operation: Raising, harvesting, or storing crops or feed,
breeding or managing livestock, including the preparation of the products
raised thereon for human use and disposed of by marketing or other means. It
includes, but is not limited to, agriculture, grazing, horticulture, forestry,
and dairy farming.
   Apartment: Any building containing more than four (4) contiguous dwelling
units or any group of buildings or mobile homes located on a single parcel that
contains a total of six (6) or more dwelling units regardless of ownership of
the dwelling units.
   Bulk Waste ("Bulk Items"): Large appliances, air conditioners, furniture,
mattresses, box springs, yard furniture, large toys, grills, push mowers,
bicycles, and playground equipment. The following items are not considered bulk
waste: Gym/exercise equipment, pianos, organs, pool tables, electronics, riding
mowers, automotive equipment, fencing, decks, swimming pools (any size except
small form plastic pools), animal shelters, demolition debris, building debris
and any other item of such weight that two adults cannot easily lift.
   Bulk Waste Container (a.k.a. - “Roll Off container”): A manufactured
container suitable for emptying by mechanical equipment.
   Class Three Waste: Non-hazardous commercial and industrial wastes that are
permitted by SCDHEC to be disposed of in a Class Three landfill. See also:
Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) and Garbage.
   Class Two Waste: The waste streams listed in Appendix I, Acceptable Waste
for Class Two Landfills, of SC Regulation 61-107.19, and Solid Waste
Management: Solid Waste Landfills and Structural Fill. The list will be posted
at each County disposal facility. See also: Construction and Demolition (C&D)
Waste.
   Code: The Richland County, South Carolina Code of Ordinances.
   Collection Area: A quasi-official subdivided area of the County for the
purpose of solid waste management program administration.
   Commercial Establishment: Any hotel, apartment, rooming house, business,
industrial, public or semi-public establishment of any nature. See also:
Apartment.
   Commercial Waste: Trash and garbage generated by apartments, operation of
stores, offices, restaurants and other places of business and industrial
establishments (excluding industrial waste as defined herein).
   Construction and Demolition (C&D) debris: Any discarded solid wastes
resulting from construction, remodeling, repair, and demolition of structures,
and road construction. The wastes include, but are not limited to, bricks,
concrete, other masonry materials, lumber, road spoils, and paving materials,
but do not include solid waste from agricultural operations or Garbage.
   Contaminant/Contamination: Generally applied in the context of recycling.
Items, to include plastic bags, garbage, or items not approved for the County's
Recycling Program, intermingled with items intended for pickup. The presence of
this contamination may preclude pickup, causing an interruption of efficient
collection operations. See also: "Non-compliant Pile/Roll Cart", "Mixed Pile",
and "Mixed Waste."
   County: Richland County, South Carolina.
   County Administrator: The Richland County Administrator.
   County Council: The governing body of Richland County, South Carolina.
   Curbside: The area within the right-of-way or easement immediately adjacent
to a public road, highway, street, etc. For purposes of this ordinance chapter,
curbside will be considered as the area within six (6) feet of the edge of the
public road, highway, and street, etc., unless deemed otherwise by the
Director. Curbside shall not extend past the road right-of-way or easement
except in those cases where the road right-of-way or easement ends at the edge
of the traveled way of the road.
   Curbside Collector: (a.k.a. - Collections Contractor) the person that has
entered into a contract with the County to provide specified solid waste
curbside collection services. The solid wastes eligible for curbside service
from dwelling units and small businesses are: garbage, household waste, yard
waste, recyclables, bulk items, and white goods as defined herein.
   Debris: Includes, but is not limited to, miscellaneous equipment, yard toys,
furniture, packaging items, shipping containers, waste tires, construction and
demolition (C&D) waste, bricks, blocks, concrete, asphalt, metals, lumber,
trees, tree limbs, tree stumps, brush or parts thereof, or stumps, and/or
building materials or solid waste of any description that are deemed by the
Director or designee to be a nuisance, potentially deleterious to public
health, public sanitation and/or public safety.
   Department: The Richland County Department of Public Works.
   DHEC: The South Carolina Department of Health and Environmental Control.
   Director: The Richland County Director of Public Works.
   Disposal: The discharge, deposition, injection, dumping, spilling, or
placing of any solid waste into or on any land or water, whether intentional or
unintentional, so that the substance or any constituent thereof may enter the
environment or be emitted into the air or discharged into any waters, including
groundwater.
   Disposal Facility: All contiguous land, structures, other appurtenances and
improvements on the land used for treating, storing, or disposing of solid
waste pursuant to a solid waste disposal permit issued by DHEC. A facility may
consist of several treatment, storage, or disposal operational units,
including, but not limited to, one or more landfills, surface impoundments, or
combination thereof.
   Domicile: A residential dwelling to include single and multi-family
configurations.
   Dumpster: A type of movable waste container designed to be brought and taken
away by a special collection vehicle, or to a bin that a specially designed
garbage truck lifts, empties into its hopper, and lowers, on the spot. The word
is a generic trademark of Dumpster, an American brand name for a specific
design.
   Dwelling unit: One or more habitable rooms which are intended to be occupied
by one (1) family with facilities for living, sleeping, cooking, and eating and
from which the County would collect solid waste; excludes commercial,
industrial and manufacturing establishments.
   Garbage: All accumulations of animal, fruit or vegetable matter that attend
the preparation, use, cooking and dealing in, or storage of meats, fish, fowl,
fruit, vegetables and any other matter of any nature whatsoever which is
subject to decay, putrefaction and the generation of noxious and offensive
smells or odors, or which during and after decay may serve as breeding or
feeding material for flies and/or germ-carrying insects or vermin; bottles.
cans or food containers which due to their ability to retain water can serve as
a breeding place for mosquitoes and other water-breeding insects.
   Hazardous waste: Those wastes that are defined as hazardous in Section 44-
56-20 of the South Carolina Hazardous Waste Management Act.
   Household: One or more people who occupy a dwelling unit as their usual
place of residence.
   Household Hazardous Waste: Any commonly used household hazardous material
that is not regulated as hazardous waste when disposed of. This includes, but
is not limited to, insecticides, pesticides, petroleum-based paints,
lubricants, fertilizers, cleaning agents and polishing compounds. For purposes
of this definition, household hazardous waste does not include gasoline or
motor oil.
   Household Quantities: Quantities of solid waste reasonably generated in the
course of typical daily domestic activities from a dwelling unit. Household
quantities typically would fit into the assigned roll cart.
